newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends down despite Egypt's purchase.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends down despite Egypt's purchase.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed lower despite news Egypt over the weekend bought at least 200,000 tonnes of wheat from the United States, traders said.
There were some ideas Egypt would buy from 500,000 tonnes to one million tonnes, so the weekend business gave a bearish spin to U.S. wheat futures markets.
There was news Pakistan this week would purchase optional-origin wheat with possibly 300,000 tonnes out of a 500,000 tonne tender coming from the U.S.
"Egypt bought and Pakistan will buy so where do we go from here? It was a quiet close and a disappointing close," a trader said.
Signals the wheat market was technically overbought after last week's rally lent pressure to prices, the traders said.
Technicians pointed to the failure of September to move into a chart gap of $3.72-1/2 to $3.74-1/2 which was set on June 16 as central to the late slide in prices.
"It failed at that level again so technically it put us on slippery ground," a trader said.
KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed 2-3/4 cents lower to 1/2 higher, with September down 2-1/2 at $3.65.
KCBT wheat futures volume was estimated by the KCBT at 39,450 contracts, above the 33,500 contracts traded Friday.
